newsitem.title: FRANCE: French source denies Italy EMU support withdrawal.
newsitem.headline: French source denies Italy EMU support withdrawal.

text.p: A government source on Friday denied a report that President Jacques Chirac had recently told German Chancellor Helmut Kohl he had withdrawn support for Italy's drive to join European monetary union.
"It's a formal denial, it's a groundless rumour," said the source, asking not to be identified.

"France's position on the choice of member countries of European monetary union is still that decided in Madrid (European Union summit) in December 1995: The choice of member countries will be made in 1998," the government source said.

The source was responding to a media report citing unnamed officials of the German CDU party as saying Chirac had shifted the emphasis away from supporting Italy's drive to become a starting member of the single European currency, the euro, in January 1999.
The report said the officials had said there was no signed agreement but that this was what Chirac had told Kohl.
